newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares up, but gains seen short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares up, but gains seen short-lived.

text.p: Slovenian shares rose 0.74 on Friday, pushed higher by a ten percent jump in food maker Droga after the company said on Thursday its 1996 net profit had risen 30 percent.
But traders cautioned the advance was bound to be short-lived as long as foreign investors, the key influence on the country's fledgling bourse, kept a low profile.
The 11-share SBI index rose 10.06 points to close at 1,377.7, halting its four-day decline. Over the week, the index has lost 3.73 percent.

"Droga was by far the main player today. But I think the overall lull on the market will continue until foreign investors definitively return to our market," said Andrej Potocnik, a trader at brokerage BPH.

The central bank last month put a damper on foreign enthusiasm for Slovenian shares when it ordered outside investors wanting to trade in the country's securities to open custodian accounts at local banks.
The index has slumped 16.8 percent since the announcement, which prompted many foreigners to bail out of the market.
Turnover inched up to 82.1 million tolars from 54.6 million. Overall three shares rose, eight fell and four were unchanged, while 11 were untraded.
"There is no demand on the market, it seems like everybody is waiting for prices to reach their bottom and then will start buying," Potocnik added.
Drug maker Lek's A issue was the most active share today, easing 0.55 percent to 27,020 tolars on volume of 920 shares for total turnover 24.9 million tolars.
Food maker Droga was the biggest gainer, jumping 10 percent to 26,400 tolars on volume of 611 shares for total turnover of 16.1 million tolars.
Hipotekarna Bank Brezice's preferred shares led the day's decliners, falling 9.98 percent to 3,590 tolars on volume of 140 shares. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
